tree.heading: In general
tree.text: The Secretary may assess the water resources needs of river basins and watersheds of the United States, including needs relating to—

tree.heading: Cooperation
tree.text: An assessment under subsection (a) shall be carried out in cooperation and coordination with—

children.text: the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency; and
the heads of other appropriate agencies.

tree.heading: Consultation
tree.text: In carrying out an assessment under subsection (a), the Secretary shall consult with Federal, tribal, State, interstate, and local governmental entities.

tree.heading: Priority river basins and watersheds
tree.text: In selecting river basins and watersheds for assessment under this section, the Secretary shall give priority to—

children.text: Sauk River Basin, Snohomish and Skagit Counties, Washington;
White River Basin, Arkansas and Missouri;

New York-New Jersey Watershed Basin, which encompasses all the watersheds that flow into the New York-New Jersey Harbor and their associated estuaries, including the Hudson, Mohawk, Raritan, Passaic, Hackensack, and Bronx River Watersheds and the Hudson River Estuary;
Chattahoochee River Basin, Alabama, Florida, and Georgia;
Connecticut River Watershed, Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and Vermont;
Lower Rouge River Watershed, Michigan; and

tree.heading: Acceptance of contributions
tree.text: In carrying out an assessment under subsection (a), the Secretary may accept contributions, in cash or in kind, from Federal, tribal, State, interstate, and local governmental entities to the extent that the Secretary determines that the contributions will facilitate completion of the assessment.

children.heading: Non-Federal share
children.text: The non-Federal share of the costs of an assessment carried out under this section on or after December 11, 2000, shall be 25 percent.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Subject to subparagraph (B), the Secretary may credit toward the non-Federal share of an assessment under this section the cost of services, materials, supplies, or other in-kind contributions provided by the non-Federal interests for the assessment.

children.heading: Maximum amount of credit
children.text: The credit under subparagraph (A) may not exceed an amount equal to 25 percent of the costs of the assessment.

tree.heading: Feasibility report on project specific recommendations from assessments

children.heading: In general
children.text: At the request of a non-Federal interest for an assessment completed under this section, the Secretary is authorized to prepare a feasibility report, in accordance with the requirements of section 2282 of this title, recommending the construction or modification of a water resources development project to address a water resources need of a river basin or watershed of the United States identified in the assessment.

children.heading: Priority watersheds
children.text: In carrying out this subsection, the Secretary shall give priority to—

the watersheds of the island of Maui, Hawaii, including the Wahikuli, Honoko̅wai, Kahana, Honokahua, and Honolua watersheds, including the coral reef habitat north of Lahaina off the northwestern coast of the island of Maui; and
the watersheds of the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, and Guam.
